parsed.title: Discussion on tax shortcuts, domain purchase, and low‑profit app idea

topics.title: Using aunt Svetlana to reduce tax penalties

claims.text: Paying aunt Svetlana 500 UAH helped avoid larger penalties by having her re‑file declarations.
The inspector ignored the author's declarations for 1.5 years and was later reprimanded, leading to a thorough check of all years.
With Svetlana's help the author paid about 1000 UAH instead of the full fines.

topics.title: Funding a domain purchase with tax calculator earnings

claims.text: User U2 mentions not having bought a domain yet.
User U1 suggests that buying a tax calculator could generate money for a domain.
User U4 doubts anyone will buy a domain for this purpose.

topics.title: Low profitability of a simple web app

claims.text: Web is the easiest platform but far less profitable than Android/iOS.
SEO is poor; even on the 10th Google page the site is not found.
No external traffic sources (Instagram, Threads, contextual ads) are available.
User acquisition is near zero because a paywall appears within the first seconds.
Conversion is presumed zero; the product offers little simplification and lacks integrations.
Successful cases involve fast delivery (< 1 week) and cross‑platform stacks like Flutter.
U4 questions the seriousness of the effort, likening it to a scam.
U1 doubts anyone would buy the app, betting on a low chance of sales.
The tax calculator works only with Ukrainian‑hryvnia FOPs; the author had to convert transactions using daily exchange rates.

topics.title: Questions about source code access and password

claims.text: U4 says the app’s source code is hidden and the only password is stored locally as a 100 % discount promo code.
U1 asks if the password can be found by searching the source code.
U4 replies sarcastically that they did not pay 299 UAH for it.
U5 labels the app as a pirated bundle.
U1 predicts most LinkedIn users could hack the app easily.
